title: Mood Indigo

trivia: What made it famous is the odd trio voicing of muted trumpet, muted trombone and low-register clarinet. Ellington's band cut it for several labels within weeks in late 1930, and it became his signature slow number.

Personnel is the core band from Wikipedia plus the standard 1930 line-up (full sax/brass roster not re-verified). Duration approximate (not taken from a source).

trivia: The band could not record it earlier because of the 1942 to 1944 musicians' strike; once the strike ended it became Doris Day's first number one. Its release coincided with the end of the war in Europe, and it became an unofficial homecoming theme for veterans.
